title: Beating Frequencies
description: Two tones of nearly equal frequency add up to a swelling and fading wave; the loudness pulses at the difference of the two frequencies.

title: Doppler Effect
description: A moving source drops sound wavefronts at successive positions; they bunch up ahead, raising the pitch, and spread out behind, lowering it.

title: Harmonic Overtones
description: The same string vibrates as one loop, two loops, three loops: each overtone adds a node and doubles or triples the fundamental frequency.

title: Sound Wave as Compression
description: A speaker cone pushes layers of air together and apart; bands of compression and rarefaction travel outward while the air itself only jiggles back and forth.

title: Standing Wave
description: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in three loops: nodes stay still, antinodes swing, and one wavelength spans two loops.

title: Binary star orbit
description: Two stars of unequal mass circle a point between them; the lighter star travels the wider path, the heavier the smaller one.

title: Comet tail
description: A comet swings round the Sun on a long ellipse. Its tail grows near the Sun and always points away from it, blown by sunlight and the solar wind, so it leads the comet outbound.

title: Exoplanet transit light curve
description: A dark planet crosses the face of its star while the star's measured brightness dips; the dip betrays the planet.

title: Expanding universe
description: A slice of space sweeps forward in time from the big bang, widening as it goes. The galaxies stay at their places in space, yet the distances between them all grow.

title: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
description: Stars plotted by temperature and brightness fall into families: a diagonal main sequence, bright giants above, faint white dwarfs below.

title: Kepler's second law of equal areas
description: A planet on an elliptical orbit sweeps out equal areas in equal times, so it races past the Sun and lingers far away.

title: Lunar eclipse
description: The Moon drifts through the long shadow cast by Earth and darkens; sunlight is blocked when Sun, Earth and Moon line up.

title: Moon phases
description: The Moon at eight points on its orbit: half of it is always lit by the Sun, but from Earth we see more or less of that lit half.

title: Ocean tides from the Moon
description: The Moon's pull raises two ocean bulges on opposite sides of Earth; as the planet turns beneath them, a shore passes through high and low tides.

title: Planetary retrograde motion
description: Earth on its inner orbit overtakes Mars; the line of sight through Mars sweeps backward, so against the stars Mars seems to stop, reverse and loop.

title: Pulsar lighthouse
description: A spinning neutron star's magnetic axis is tilted off its spin axis, so its two beams sweep the sky like a lighthouse, and an observer they cross records a regular train of pulses.

title: Seasons from axial tilt
description: Earth keeps its axis tilted 23.5 degrees in the same direction all year, so each hemisphere leans toward or away from the Sun as it orbits.

title: Solar eclipse
description: The Moon steps between Sun and Earth; its small dark shadow sweeps across the Earth's surface and briefly hides the Sun.

title: Solar system orbits
description: Four planets circle the Sun on concentric paths; the nearer a planet is to the Sun, the faster it completes its orbit.

title: Spiral galaxy
description: Two arms wind out of a bright bulge across a tilted disc. Inner stars lap faster than the arms, which turn as a slow wave of density that stars pass through.

title: Stellar life cycle
description: A sun-like star's life in order: a gas nebula, a steady star, a swollen red giant that sheds a shell, and a fading white dwarf.

title: Stellar parallax
description: As Earth circles the Sun, the line of sight through a near star sweeps across the distant stars. The star seems to trace a small yearly ellipse, and its width gives the distance.

title: Supernova explosion
description: A star's core collapses to a bright remnant while shock fronts and streaks of gas race outward, seeding space with the elements the star made.

title: ATP synthase
description: Protons flowing down their gradient through ATP synthase spin its rotor and shaft; the turning head squeezes ADP and phosphate together into ATP.

title: Bacteriophage injecting DNA
description: A T4-like phage stands on a bacterium on its tail fibres; the sheath contracts, driving the tube through the cell wall, and viral DNA runs from capsid into the cell.

title: Bee waggle dance
description: On the comb a bee traces a figure-eight; the angle of its straight waggle run from vertical tells the hive the direction of food relative to the sun.

title: Binary fission
description: A rod-shaped bacterium that has copied its DNA lays down a septum across its middle, then the two halves round off their new poles and part as identical daughters.

title: Butterfly Metamorphosis
description: Eggs on a leaf, a caterpillar inching along a twig, a chrysalis swaying beneath it and a butterfly beating its wings: one animal rebuilt in four stages.

title: Cell membrane
description: A bilayer of phospholipids, heads out and tails in, studded with a channel protein through which an ion passes down its gradient.

title: Chloroplast
description: Inside a chloroplast's double envelope, stacks of thylakoid discs catch incoming light in their grana while sugars built in the stroma drift out.

title: Echolocating Bat
description: A bat in flight sends out rings of ultrasound; they strike a moth and dashed echoes ripple back, and the delay tells the bat how far away its prey is flying.

title: Endocytosis
description: Reading left to right, the cell membrane dimples under bound cargo, deepens into a coated pit, nearly closes at the neck, and a sealed vesicle drifts into the cell.

title: Enzyme lock and key
description: A substrate whose shape matches the enzyme's active site slots in, is converted, and is released as two products, leaving the enzyme unchanged.

title: Bacterial flagellum motor
description: A rotary motor set in a bacterial envelope: protons passing through fixed stators spin the rings and rod, and the helical filament corkscrews out behind.

title: Golgi apparatus and secretion
description: Vesicles from the ER join the stacked sacs of the Golgi at one face; finished cargo buds off the other and crosses the cell to spill out through the membrane.

title: Krebs cycle
description: The citric acid cycle as a wheel of carbon skeletons: a two-carbon acetyl joins four to make six, then two carbons leave as CO₂ and the four-carbon carrier returns.

title: Leaf Stomata
description: A leaf pore seen under the microscope: two guard cells swell and part, letting carbon dioxide in and water vapour out, then slacken and close. Every breath costs water.

title: Mitochondrion
description: A mitochondrion has a smooth outer membrane and a deeply folded inner membrane; the cristae enlarge the surface where ATP is made and released.

title: Mitosis (anaphase)
description: In anaphase the spindle fibres shorten and pull the separated sister chromatids toward opposite poles, so each daughter cell gets one full copy.

title: Osmosis in cells
description: Water crosses the membrane toward the saltier side: a cell in dilute water swells, while one in salty water loses water and shrinks.

title: Photosynthesis
description: A leaf turns sunlight, water from the roots and carbon dioxide from the air into sugar, and releases oxygen.

title: Phototropism
description: A seedling bends toward the light: auxin gathers on the shaded side of the stem, those cells elongate, and the shoot curves toward the sun.

title: Plant cell
description: A plant cell: rigid wall, a great central vacuole and a nucleus at the edge, with chloroplasts carried around the vacuole by the streaming cytoplasm.

title: Pollination
description: A bee carries pollen from one flower to another as it feeds, fertilising the blooms along the way; the dotted arc is its route.

title: Protein folding
description: A loose chain of residues collapses on itself: water-shy beads (filled) bury into a hydrophobic core while polar beads (open) stay on the outside.

title: Seed dispersal by wind
description: A dandelion head releases parachute seeds that drift away on the wind while a maple key spins down: plants send seeds far from the parent.

title: Sodium-potassium pump
description: Powered by ATP, a membrane pump carries three sodium ions out of the cell and two potassium ions in, against their concentration gradients.

title: Transcription by RNA polymerase
description: RNA polymerase slides along DNA, opening a small bubble and copying one strand into a growing messenger RNA that peels away behind it.

title: Translation on the ribosome
description: A ribosome slides along messenger RNA, matching tRNA anticodons to codons and linking amino acids into a growing polypeptide chain.

title: Tree Rings
description: A trunk in cross-section lays down one ring a year, wide when wet and narrow in drought; as the newest ring spreads outward, the same years are read off as a bar chart.

title: Atomic orbitals s, p and d
description: The s orbital is a sphere, p a pair of lobes along an axis, d a four-leaf clover: the shapes of the regions where an electron is likely to be found.

title: Benzene ring with delocalised electrons
description: Six carbons form a flat hexagon; the electrons of its double bonds are not fixed but spread as a ring of charge circling the whole molecule.

title: Bohr atom model
description: Electrons circle a nucleus on fixed orbits; when one falls to a lower orbit it emits a photon, so atomic energy comes in discrete steps.

title: A catalyst lowers the energy barrier
description: Two routes from reactants to products: the dashed hill is the uncatalysed climb, the lower solid one is the catalysed route, so more molecules get over.

title: Chemical equilibrium
description: Reactant and product concentrations change until they level off; the arrows keep trading both ways at equal rates, a balance that is dynamic.

title: Paper chromatography
description: A solvent creeps up a plate and carries a mixture with it; each component rises at its own speed, so the mixture separates into distinct spots.

title: Covalent bond in a hydrogen molecule
description: Two hydrogen atoms overlap their orbitals so that a pair of electrons circles both nuclei: the bond is a shared pair.

title: Ionic crystal lattice
description: Sodium and chloride ions alternate in a regular grid, each held by its neighbours; heat only makes them tremble about fixed positions.

title: Electrolysis of water
description: A battery drives current through two electrodes in water, splitting it: oxygen bubbles form at one electrode and twice as much hydrogen at the other.

title: Fractional distillation column
description: Heated crude oil enters a tall column; vapours rise and condense on trays at different heights, so light fractions leave at the top and heavy ones low down.

title: Galvanic cell
description: Zinc dissolves as ions and sends electrons through the wire to a copper electrode, where copper ions take them up; a salt bridge completes the circuit.

title: Hydrogen bonding between water molecules
description: Water molecules jostle while dashed hydrogen bonds link a hydrogen on one molecule to the oxygen of its neighbour, flickering as they form and break.

title: Ionic bond: sodium gives an electron to chlorine
description: Sodium hands its single outer electron to chlorine; the resulting positive and negative ions are held together by electrostatic attraction.

title: The pH scale from acid to base
description: A scale from 0 to 14: many hydrogen ions (filled dots) at the acid end, many hydroxide ions (open rings) at the basic end, and a balance at neutral 7.

title: Reaction energy profile
description: A ball climbs the activation-energy hill between reactants and products, then rolls down to a lower level; the drop is the energy released.

title: Acid–base titration
description: Base drips from a burette into acid in a flask while the pH curve climbs slowly, then leaps at the equivalence point where the two exactly cancel.

title: Tetrahedral molecular geometry of methane
description: Four bonding pairs repel one another as far apart as possible, so methane takes a tetrahedral shape with bond angles of 109.5 degrees; wedges point toward you.

title: Water is a polar molecule
description: A bent water molecule has partial negative charge on oxygen and partial positive on its hydrogens; between charged plates it turns to line up.

title: The carbon cycle
description: Carbon dioxide moves between atmosphere, plants, ocean and buried fossil carbon: plants and seas draw it down, while respiration and burning fuel return it to the air.

title: Cold front
description: A wedge of dense cold air ploughs under warm air like a snowplough, forcing it upward until it condenses into a towering storm cloud and rain.

title: Coriolis effect
description: On the turning Earth the equator moves faster than the high latitudes, so air heading for it falls behind: winds bend right in the north, left in the south.

title: El Niño
description: A slice across the Pacific: the trade winds hold warm water and its rain clouds in the west; when they slacken, the warm pool sloshes east and the thermocline goes flat.

title: Greenhouse effect
description: Sunlight warms the surface, which radiates infrared; greenhouse gas molecules in the atmosphere absorb some and send it back down, trapping heat.

title: Hurricane structure
description: A hurricane seen from above: spiral rain bands wind counterclockwise around a ring of towering storm clouds, the eyewall, that encloses a calm clear eye.

title: Milankovitch cycles
description: Three slow rhythms of Earth's orbit that pace the ice ages: its ellipse stretches, its tilt nods, its axis wobbles, each beating at its own period.

title: Thermohaline circulation
description: The ocean conveyor: warm surface water flows to the poles, cools and sinks, and returns as cold deep water, driven by differences in temperature and salt.

title: Attention mechanism
description: To read the word it, a model weighs every earlier word: even arcs and bars gather into a peak on animal, and meaning flows along that arc. Attention, the heart of a transformer.

title: Binary counter
description: Four columns of dots worth 8, 4, 2 and 1 light up as a counter climbs from 0 to 15; each bit flips half as often as the one beside it.

title: Binary search
description: A pointer jumps to the middle of a sorted row of bars, discards the half that cannot hold the target, and repeats until it lands on it: logarithmic search.

title: Breadth-first search
description: A dashed frontier sweeps outward from the start node of a graph, visiting every node one step away, then two steps, then three: breadth-first traversal.

title: Bubble sort
description: Five bars of different heights are sorted by repeatedly comparing neighbours and swapping those out of order, so the tallest bar bubbles to the right.

title: Rule 30 cellular automaton
description: A single black cell grows into a chaotic triangle, each new row set by a simple rule applied to three cells above; the moving frame shows one such update.

title: Game of Life glider
description: On the Game of Life grid a five-cell glider cycles through four shapes while crawling one cell diagonally every four generations, motion born of simple rules.

title: Gradient descent
description: A ball steps downhill across the contour lines of a loss surface, zigzagging with shrinking steps toward the minimum, as an optimiser follows the negative gradient.

title: Hash table
description: Keys pass through a hash function that scatters each one to a bucket in an array; the dots follow their key to its slot, giving constant-time lookup.

title: K-means clustering
description: Three centroids start in the wrong places; each point joins its nearest, each centroid steps to the mean of its points, and after a few rounds the three natural clusters emerge.

title: Logic gate (AND)
description: An AND gate with two input wires and one output: signals light up the wires in turn, and the output only glows when both inputs are on.

title: Neural network forward pass
description: Activations flow left to right through layers of a small neural network; each wave of light is a layer's outputs feeding the next layer's inputs.

title: Public-key cryptography
description: A padlock with two keys: the public key can only snap it shut, scrambling the message inside, and only the matching private key can open it again. Asymmetric encryption.

title: Recursion and the call stack
description: Each recursive call stacks a new frame on the last until the base case is reached, then the answer travels back down as the frames are popped off one by one.

title: Turing machine
description: A head with a state reads a cell of an endless tape, writes a new symbol, and steps one cell along; this rule-following is all that computation needs.

title: Layers of the Earth
description: Concentric layers of the Earth: a thin crust, the thick mantle, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core, with slow circulation in the mantle and core.

title: Fossils in rock strata
description: Sediment settles in layers, burying creatures as fossils: the deepest layers and fossils are the oldest, the shallowest the youngest.

title: Hotspot island chain
description: A fixed mantle plume feeds one active volcano while the plate drifts over it, leaving a chain of ever older, lower and more eroded islands behind.

title: Plate subduction
description: A dense oceanic plate slides beneath a continental plate at a trench and sinks into the mantle, melting as it descends and feeding a volcano above.

title: River meander
description: Seen from above, a river swings in loops, eroding the outer bank and dropping sediment on the inner bend; a cut-off loop is left behind as an oxbow lake.

title: The rock cycle
description: Magma cools to igneous rock, weathering turns it to sedimentary rock, heat and pressure make metamorphic rock, and melting returns it to magma: rock as an endless loop.

title: Seismic waves from an earthquake
description: Rings spread from an earthquake's epicentre to a station, where the seismograph records the fast P wave first, then the larger S wave and surface waves.

title: Tsunami wave
description: A seafloor earthquake lifts the water; the long, low wave races across the ocean, then slows, shortens and grows tall as the seabed shoals toward the coast.

title: Volcanic eruption
description: Cross-section of a volcano: magma rises from its chamber through the conduit and erupts as lava, ash and flying bombs.

title: The water cycle
description: Sun-warmed sea water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as rain on the mountains and runs back to the sea in rivers: water in an endless loop.

title: Ant Trail Pheromones
description: Ants carry food along the shorter way round a stone: more trips lay more scent, more scent draws more ants, while the long route evaporates. No ant knows the map.

title: Bird Flocking
description: A murmuration of starlings wheels as one while a turn ripples through it; each bird tracks only its seven nearest neighbours, and the flock emerges with no leader.

title: Ecological Succession
description: Lichen on bare rock gives way to grass, flowers, shrubs, birch and finally oak, each stage growing in turn and building the deeper soil that the next one needs.

title: Food web
description: A small food web: arrows run from the eaten to the eater, so energy from grass and berries passes to herbivores, carnivores and a top predator.

title: Logistic population growth
description: A population grows slowly, then fast, then levels off at the carrying capacity K where resources run out: the S-shaped logistic curve.

title: Mycorrhizal Network
description: Beneath a forest floor, threads of fungus link the roots of separate trees; sugars travel from a big tree in the light through the hyphae to a seedling in its shade.

title: Nitrogen Cycle
description: Air nitrogen is fixed in the root nodules of a legume, turned by soil bacteria to ammonium and nitrate, drunk by plants, returned by decay and finally released as gas.

title: Predator-prey cycle
description: Prey and predator numbers rise and fall in lagged waves: more prey feeds more predators, who then cut the prey back, and the cycle repeats.

title: Trophic pyramid
description: Energy pyramid: each feeding level holds roughly a tenth of the energy of the one below, so producers are many and top predators few.

title: Compound interest
description: Two savers start together: one earns interest only on the original sum, the other on interest too, so the exponential curve and its growing dot pull away from the straight line.

title: Prisoner's dilemma
description: A two-by-two payoff grid where each player does better by defecting whatever the other does, so a marker of best replies slides to mutual defection even though cooperating pays both more.

title: Supply and demand
description: A rising supply curve and a falling demand curve cross at the market price; when demand shifts, the crossing point slides along the supply curve to a new price and quantity.

title: Hydroelectric Dam
description: Water held high behind a dam falls through a penstock to spin a turbine, turning stored gravitational energy into electricity sent out along the grid.

title: Nuclear Chain Reaction
description: A neutron splits a uranium nucleus into two fragments and frees more neutrons; each splits another nucleus in turn, so one fission becomes two, then four: a self-sustaining chain reaction.

title: Solar Cell p–n Junction
description: A photon strikes the junction between n-type and p-type silicon, freeing an electron and a hole that are driven apart, so electrons flow through the external load.

title: Wind Turbine
description: Moving air turns a three-bladed rotor on a tower; the power captured grows with the swept area and with the cube of the wind speed.

title: Feedback Control Loop
description: A controller compares a measured output with the set-point and drives the process to shrink the error; the sensor closes the loop and the response settles on target.

title: Four-Stroke Engine
description: A piston, connecting rod and crank cycle through intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes while the valves open in turn and a spark ignites the charge.

title: Gear Train
description: Three meshing gears turn in alternating directions; the smaller the gear, the faster it spins, so speed and torque trade off in proportion to the tooth counts.

title: Hydraulic Press
description: A small piston pushing on an enclosed fluid raises a much larger piston: pressure is shared, so force scales with piston area while the distance moved shrinks.

title: Lever and Fulcrum
description: A plank pivots on a fulcrum; a small push on the long arm balances a heavy load on the short arm, because load times its distance equals effort times its distance.

title: Pulley System
description: A rope runs from a beam under a moving pulley and over a fixed one: pull the free end down by 2d and the load rises only d, so two rope runs share the weight and the force is halved.

title: Truss Bridge
description: A road deck rides on a triangulated truss: a vehicle's weight is carried as compression along the top chord and tension along the bottom chord and diagonals.

title: Adaptive radiation of finch beaks
description: From one ancestral bird, lineages fan out into new niches; each descendant's beak is shaped for a different food, so one form radiates into many.

title: Convergent evolution: shark and dolphin
description: A fish and a mammal, only distantly related, evolved the same streamlined body for fast swimming: similar form shaped by the same pressure, not by shared descent.

title: Fossils changing through rock strata
description: Rock layers stack oldest at the bottom; shells found in successive layers grow larger and more coiled, a record of one lineage changing gradually through time.

title: Genetic drift in a small population
description: Allele frequencies wander by chance each generation; in a small population some lines drift all the way to loss or fixation without any selection.

title: Horizontal gene transfer between bacteria
description: One bacterium passes a loop of DNA, a plasmid, through a thin bridge into another cell, so genes move sideways between unrelated lineages rather than parent to child.

title: Natural selection shifting a trait
description: Individuals with a favoured trait leave more offspring, so over generations the whole distribution of that trait slides toward the advantaged end.

title: Peppered moth and industrial melanism
description: On pale birch bark pale moths hide and dark ones get eaten; once soot darkens the trunks the odds reverse, and dark moths come to dominate.

title: Phylogenetic tree of descent
description: A branching tree traces how six species descend from shared ancestors; each fork is a common ancestor, and branch order records how recently lineages split.

title: Chromosome structure and chromatin packing
description: A chromosome zoomed in is chromatin: DNA wrapped around histone spools, the nucleosomes, like beads on a string, packed ever tighter to fit a cell.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing
description: A guide RNA leads the Cas9 enzyme to a matching stretch of DNA, where it makes a clean cut across both strands so the gene can be changed.

title: DNA double helix
description: Two backbones twist around one axis with base-pair rungs between them; as the helix turns, rungs lengthen and shorten and the beads swing front to back.

title: DNA replication fork
description: The parent duplex unzips at a fork; helicase opens it and polymerases build a new strand against each old template, so one duplex becomes two.

title: Gel electrophoresis of DNA fragments
description: An electric field pulls DNA fragments through a gel; shorter pieces slip through faster and travel farther, sorting a mixture into bands by size.

title: Gene expression: DNA to mRNA to protein
description: RNA polymerase copies a gene from DNA into messenger RNA, which carries the message to a ribosome that translates it into a chain of amino acids.

title: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
description: A unit square split by allele frequency p and q: its areas p², 2pq and q² are the genotype shares, and they stay fixed when nothing acts on the population.

title: PCR: amplifying DNA by thermal cycling
description: Repeated cycles of heating, cooling and copying double the DNA each round: one molecule becomes two, four, eight, a billion, as temperature rises and falls.

title: Point mutation
description: A single base in a gene is swapped; because codons are read in threes, that one change can alter a single amino acid in the protein built from it.

title: Punnett square
description: Two Aa parents each give one allele; the four boxes list every combination, showing offspring in a 1 : 2 : 1 ratio of AA, Aa and aa.

title: Bézier curve by de Casteljau's construction
description: Four control points, and points sliding along the lines between them, again and again: the last one left traces the smooth cubic Bézier curve.

title: Cycloid traced by a rolling wheel
description: A wheel rolls along a line without slipping while one point on its rim traces a cycloid: a row of arches, touching the ground in cusps.

title: Golden spiral
description: A golden rectangle breaks into ever smaller squares, and quarter-circle arcs through them wind into a spiral that grows by the golden ratio every quarter turn.

title: Inscribed angle theorem
description: A point glides around a circle while its rays stay pinned to a chord's ends: the angle it sees never changes, and is always half the angle at the centre.

title: Koch snowflake
description: Every side is replaced by four sides a third as long, again and again: the outline grows without bound while the snowflake's area stays finite.

title: Möbius strip
description: A strip with a half twist: a walker on it goes round twice, solid on the near face and hollow beneath, and returns home having crossed no edge. It has one side.

title: Pi as an unrolled circle
description: A circle rolls through one turn along a line and lays down its circumference, which spans three diameters and a little more: that ratio is pi.

title: Pythagorean theorem
description: Squares drawn on the sides of a 3-4-5 right triangle: the unit cells of the two small squares move across to exactly fill the square on the hypotenuse.

title: Sierpinski triangle
description: A triangle with its middle removed, again and again in every remaining corner; a dot hopping halfway to random corners lands only on this self-similar fractal.

title: Copernican model
description: Two cosmos side by side: Ptolemy's Earth-centred sky needs a planet looping on an epicycle, while Copernicus puts the Sun in the middle and the loops give way to plain circles.

title: Galileo's inclined plane
description: A ball rolls down Galileo's ramp past frets set so it reaches one at each equal beat: the distances run 1, 3, 5, 7, the times-squared law of falling bodies.

title: Language family tree
description: A reconstructed proto-word, dashed where nothing was written down, branches into daughter languages; dots carry it down the tree until it arrives as father in one and padre in another.

title: Syntax tree
description: The sentence the cat saw a bird parsed as a tree: a clause splits into noun phrase and verb phrase, down to the words, while a ring walks the tree node by node as a parser would.

title: Crystal Dislocation
description: An edge dislocation, the end of an extra half-plane of atoms, glides along the slip plane under shear; when it leaves, the upper crystal has slipped one atom over, which is why metals bend.

title: Graphene Lattice
description: A honeycomb of carbon atoms seen from above, with electrons running freely across the mesh; below, the same sheet edge-on ripples as a single line, just one atom thick.

title: Stress–Strain Curve
description: A steel test piece is pulled while a point climbs its stress–strain curve: straight elastic rise, yield, strain hardening, then necking to fracture, where the piece parts.

title: Derivative as the slope of a tangent line
description: A tangent line slides along a curve; its rise over run is the derivative, the curve's instantaneous slope, steep on the flanks and flat at the peaks.

title: Eigenvectors of a linear transformation
description: A matrix stretches and shears the plane: most vectors are knocked off their line, but the two eigenvectors stay on theirs, only scaled by their eigenvalues.

title: Fibonacci sequence as growing generations
description: Each filled dot spawns itself and a hollow one, each hollow dot turns filled: the rows hold 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 dots, every count the sum of the two before.

title: Fourier series of a square wave
description: Three nested rotating circles, each three and five times faster and smaller, add up to trace a near-square wave: any periodic shape is a sum of sines.

title: The seven bridges of Königsberg
description: A walker crosses the seven bridges of Königsberg, each only once; the bridges used go dim, and he is stranded with one left: Euler's proof that no such walk exists.

title: Sequence converging to a limit
description: Terms of a sequence zigzag in toward a dashed limit L; as the epsilon band around L narrows, all later terms still fall inside it.

title: Sieve of Eratosthenes finding the primes
description: The numbers 1 to 90 in a grid: take 2, 3, 5 and 7 in turn and strike out their multiples, and only the prime numbers are left standing.

title: Riemann sum approaching an integral
description: Rectangles under a curve are refined from 4 to 8 to 16 strips; their summed area closes in on the exact area, the definite integral of f.

title: Unit circle and sine wave
description: A radius turns round the unit circle while its height is unrolled into a sine wave: sin θ is the vertical shadow of a point in circular motion.

title: Antibody and antigen
description: A Y-shaped antibody, built from paired protein domains, reaches down and clasps two matching antigens on a pathogen surface with the tips of its arms.

title: ECG heartbeat
description: An electrocardiogram trace: the small P wave, the sharp QRS spike and the rounded T wave repeat with every beat as the heart depolarises and recovers.

title: Epidemic SIR curves
description: The SIR model of an epidemic: susceptible people fall as recovered people rise, while the infected curve swells to a peak and dies away as hosts run out.

title: Heart and double circulation
description: The heart pumps twice in one circuit: spent blood from the body goes through the right heart to the lungs, then returns oxygenated to the left heart and out to the body.

title: Kidney nephron
description: One nephron of the kidney: blood is filtered at the glomerulus, and the filtrate runs through the tubule and loop of Henle, water reclaimed, into the collecting duct.

title: Gas exchange in the lung
description: An air sac of the lung wrapped by a capillary: oxygen crosses the thin wall into passing red cells, which darken as they load, while carbon dioxide leaves.

title: Muscle sarcomere
description: A sarcomere, the unit of muscle: myosin heads ratchet along thin actin filaments, drawing the Z lines inward so the whole band shortens while no filament does.

title: Peristalsis
description: Rings of muscle along the gut relax ahead of a bolus and squeeze behind it, so a travelling wave of contraction pushes the food forward along the tube.

title: Controlled experiment
description: Two identical pots on one bench measured by one ruler: only the treated plant gets the drops and it grows taller, while the untouched control shows what would have happened anyway.

title: Falsification
description: A row of white swans supports the claim that all swans are white, but no number of them proves it: one black swan gliding in strikes the sentence out. Popper's falsifiability.

title: Scientific method loop
description: The scientific method as a closed loop: observe with the eye, guess with a dashed idea, test in the flask, then back to looking again, a token walking round and never arriving.

title: Packet routing
description: A message is cut into three packets that hop from router to router by different paths, arrive out of order, and fall back into sequence at the receiver: packet switching.

title: Scale-free network
description: A few large hubs hold most of the links while most nodes hold one; each newcomer attaches to a hub, which grows larger: preferential attachment, the rich get richer.

title: Small-world network
description: A ring of neighbours crossed by a few long chords; one signal walks round the ring while another takes a shortcut and arrives in three hops, why any two people are so few steps apart.

title: Action potential
description: Membrane voltage rests, crosses a threshold, spikes sharply, overshoots below rest and recovers: the all-or-none electrical spike of a neuron.

title: Lobes of the brain
description: The brain in side view, divided by its sulci into frontal, parietal, occipital and temporal lobes, with the cerebellum and brainstem beneath.

title: Circadian rhythm
description: A 24-hour clock of the body: the hand sweeps through day and night while core temperature, drawn as a dashed ring, swells by evening and sinks before dawn.

title: Cochlea and hearing
description: The cochlea, shown coiled and then unrolled: sound sends a wave along the basilar membrane that peaks at one place, high notes near the base and low near the tip.

title: Hebbian learning
description: Two neurons fire in step, a spike running from one to the other, and the synapse between them slowly grows: cells that fire together wire together.

title: Neuron structure
description: A neuron: dendrites gather signals into the cell body, and an impulse leaps from gap to gap along the myelinated axon to its branching terminals.

title: Reflex arc
description: A sensory neuron carries a painful stimulus into the spinal cord, which answers through a motor neuron, so the muscle withdraws before the brain is involved.

title: Eye and retina
description: Light from an object is focused by the lens onto the retina, forming a small inverted image that photoreceptors turn into nerve signals.

title: Sleep cycles
description: A hypnogram of one night: sleep descends into deep stages and climbs back about every ninety minutes, deep sleep fading as dreaming REM spells lengthen.

title: Synapse and neurotransmitters
description: Vesicles in the presynaptic terminal release transmitter molecules that cross the cleft and bind receptors on the next cell, passing the signal on.

title: Converging Lens
description: Three rays leave the tip of an arrow, pass a convex lens and meet again at one point, forming an inverted real image beyond the focal point.

title: Double-Slit Interference
description: Light passes through two close slits; the two spreading wavefronts overlap and add up to a pattern of bright and dark fringes on the screen.

title: Polarization of Light
description: Light vibrating in every direction meets a polarizing filter and leaves vibrating in one plane; a second filter, crossed with the first, stops it entirely.

title: Prism Dispersion
description: White light enters a glass prism and fans into a spectrum: each wavelength bends by a slightly different angle, so one beam leaves as many.

title: Single-Slit Diffraction
description: Plane waves squeeze through a narrow slit and spread as circular wavefronts, painting a bright central band with fainter side lobes on the screen.

title: Snell's Law of Refraction
description: A ray bends toward the normal as it enters glass; its wavefronts bunch up as they slow, and the change of speed is what turns the ray.

title: Total Internal Reflection
description: A beam sweeps up under a water surface: past the critical angle the escaping ray flattens along the surface and vanishes, and all the light reflects back.

title: Bernoulli's principle
description: Fluid speeds up through a narrow neck of a pipe and the pressure there drops: the liquid column over the constriction stands lower than over the wide parts.

title: Blackbody radiation
description: Hotter bodies glow brighter and bluer: Planck's spectra peak at shorter wavelengths as temperature rises, while the classical curve (dashed) wrongly diverges.

title: Brownian motion
description: A pollen grain wanders along a jagged random walk, knocked this way and that by the unseen molecules of the fluid: the visible trace of thermal motion.

title: Buoyancy and Archimedes' principle
description: A block floats in water: the upward buoyant force equals the weight of the water the submerged part pushes aside, balancing the block's own weight.

title: Capacitor Charging
description: Current rushes through a resistor onto two parallel plates, then slows as charge piles up, so the voltage across them climbs along an exponential curve.

title: Carnot cycle
description: On a pressure-volume diagram the ideal heat engine traces a loop of two isotherms and two adiabats; the enclosed area is the work it delivers each cycle.

title: Centripetal force
description: A ball circles a centre. Its velocity points along the tangent, and an inward force along the string keeps bending its path into the circle.

title: Convection cells
description: Fluid between a hot plate and a cold one organises into counter-rotating rolls: parcels warm at the bottom, rise, cool along the top and sink again.

title: Coupled pendulums
description: Two pendulums joined by a soft spring: the swing passes wholly from one to the other and back, and the bars below show their energy trading places.

title: Double-slit experiment
description: Electrons sent one at a time through two slits land as single dots, yet build up interference fringes: matter behaves as both particle and wave.

title: Electromagnetic Induction
description: A magnet slides in and out of a coil and a meter needle swings: current flows only while the field through the coil is changing, and stops when the magnet pauses.

title: Electromagnetic Wave
description: An electric field and a magnetic field oscillate at right angles and in step, each regenerating the other, and travel together as light at speed c.

title: Entropy and diffusion
description: Gas particles, all packed into the left half of a box, spread out through the removed partition until they fill it evenly: disorder grows, entropy rises.

title: Feynman diagram
description: Two electrons approach, trade a virtual photon along a wavy line, and recoil apart. A slice of the present sweeps along the time axis, reading the diagram as a story of one force.

title: Gravitational lensing
description: A massive lens bends the light of a distant source around it, so the observer sees the source displaced to two apparent images along the dashed lines of sight.

title: Gravitational waves
description: Two compact masses orbit one another and spin out a spiral of ripples in spacetime that travel outward and fade, the gravitational waves of a merging binary.

title: Gyroscope precession
description: A spinning wheel held at one end of its axle does not fall: gravity's torque instead turns the axle slowly around the post, the precession of angular momentum.

title: Heat conduction
description: Heat flows along a metal rod from a flame to ice as atoms vibrate hardest at the hot end and pass the jostling on, so temperature falls steadily along it.

title: Ideal gas in a piston
description: Heated from below, gas molecules in a cylinder speed up and push a weighted piston higher: at constant pressure, volume grows with temperature, PV = nRT.

title: Inclined plane
description: A block slides down a ramp while its weight splits into a part along the slope, which pulls it down, and a part into the slope, which the surface carries.

title: Laminar versus turbulent flow
description: Two channels: in laminar flow, parallel layers glide smoothly, quickest in the middle; in turbulent flow, the stream breaks into swirling, tangled eddies.

title: Light cone
description: A spacetime diagram: light rays from one event bound a future and a past cone; a traveller's worldline stays inside, and regions outside are out of causal reach.

title: Magnetic Field Lines
description: Field lines loop from the north pole of a bar magnet around to the south; small compass needles drift along them, always turning to follow the line.

title: Meissner effect
description: Above its critical temperature a metal lets magnetic field lines run straight through; cooled into a superconductor it expels them, and the lines bend around an empty interior.

title: Newton's cradle
description: Five hanging balls: one swings in and strikes the row, and one ball swings out the far side. Momentum and energy pass straight through, conserved.

title: Nuclear fission
description: A neutron strikes a heavy uranium nucleus, which tears into two unequal fragments, barium and krypton, and throws out three more neutrons: the seed of a chain reaction.

title: Pair production
description: A photon passing a nucleus turns into an electron and a positron. In a magnetic field their tracks curl in opposite senses and tighten as they slow: energy made into matter.

title: Particle in a box
description: An electron trapped between two walls can only hold standing waves with whole half-wavelengths; the first three allowed states and their rising energies are shown.

title: Pendulum
description: A bob swings on a string beneath a pivot; the faint arc is the path it keeps retracing, the rhythm of simple harmonic motion.

title: Photoelectric effect
description: Light hitting a metal frees electrons only if each photon carries enough energy: low-frequency light, however it is drawn on, ejects nothing; high-frequency light does.

title: Projectile motion
description: A ball launched at an angle traces a parabola: steady sideways drift, gravity bending the vertical speed. Faint copies mark equal time steps.

title: Quantum entanglement
description: A source emits two particles with linked spins: whichever way one dial points, the far one points the opposite way, however far apart they have travelled.

title: Quantum tunneling
description: A wave packet meets an energy barrier: most of it is reflected, but a small, weaker part leaks through to the far side though classically it could not.

title: Radioactive half-life
description: An exponential decay curve falls by half in each equal interval of time, while a sample of sixteen unstable atoms decays in step: eight left, then four, two, one.

title: Resonance
description: A heavy pendulum drives a row of lighter ones from the same bar: only the one of equal length, sharing its natural frequency, builds up a wide swing.

title: Spacetime curvature
description: A mass dents the grid of spacetime into a well, and a planet circling on the slope follows the straightest path it can: gravity as geometry, not as a force.

title: Spring oscillator
description: A mass on a spring bobs up and down about its rest line; traced against time, its height becomes a sine wave, the signature of harmonic motion.

title: Stern-Gerlach spin experiment
description: Silver atoms pass through an uneven magnetic field and land in just two spots, not a smear: spin along an axis is quantised into up and down.

title: Time dilation
description: Two light clocks: the photon in the moving clock must travel a longer diagonal path, so its tick takes longer. Moving clocks run slow, here by a factor of 1.25.

title: Torque and lever
description: A beam balances on a fulcrum: a heavy weight close in and a light one far out carry equal torque, force times distance from the pivot.

title: Uncertainty principle
description: A sharp position peak needs a broad spread of momentum, and vice versa: as one bell curve narrows the other widens, so their widths can never both shrink.

title: Wave Interference
description: Ripples from two synchronised sources overlap: where crests meet they reinforce, and along the dashed nodal lines crest meets trough and the water stays calm.

title: Anchoring bias
description: Estimates cluster around the true value on a number line, but an arbitrary anchor placed further along drags them toward itself; the cluster slides toward the anchor and back.

title: Forgetting curve
description: Memory fades along an exponential curve, but each review lifts retention back to the top and slows the next decline, so spaced repetition keeps the memory alive.

title: Bayes theorem
description: A broad dashed prior belief meets the likelihood of new evidence; their product is a sharper posterior that narrows further as more evidence accumulates.

title: Central limit theorem
description: Averages drawn from a lopsided population drop one by one into a pile that settles into a symmetric bell curve, whatever the shape of the original distribution.

title: Confidence interval
description: Ten repeated samples each give an interval around their own estimate; most straddle the dashed true value, and the odd one misses it, which is what 95 percent confidence means.

title: Linear regression
description: A line swings and settles through a cloud of points, ending where the dashed vertical residuals are smallest overall: the least-squares fit.

title: Normal distribution
description: A bell curve centred on its mean; the shaded band within one standard deviation holds about 68 percent, and the dashed ghost curve breathes wider and narrower as σ changes.

title: Simpson's paradox
description: Three clusters each trend upward, yet pooled together the dashed trend falls; the view fades between the within-group lines and the misleading overall line.

title: GPS Trilateration
description: Three satellites send timed signals; each travel time gives a distance, an arc around that satellite, and the three arcs cross at one point on the ground: the receiver.

title: Laser: Stimulated Emission
description: One photon crossing a cavity makes each excited atom it passes emit an identical photon in step with it, so a coherent beam builds and leaves through the part-silvered mirror.

title: Optical Fibre
description: Pulses of light zigzag down a curving glass core, reflected at the cladding by total internal reflection so they follow the bend; an end-on view shows the core inside its cladding.

title: Transistor as a Switch
description: A MOSFET in cross-section: charge on the gate draws a conducting channel between source and drain so electrons flow; remove it and the channel closes, the on and off of every chip.
